jobs.title: Design codex — RFC 0048 Phase A handler port
jobs.objective: Design RFC 0048 Phase A port across two tracks. Track A (workflow-loop handlers): port register_session, claim_next, ack_work, complete_job, release_lease, block_job, record_verdict, submit_review, override_review_verdict from src/striatum/cli/mutations.py (SQLite-backed via striatum.db) to PG-backed handler module(s) under src/striatum/daemon_pg/handlers/; swap DaemonRpcRouter._route delegation for these methods to call the PG handlers directly. Track B (recovery + evidence handlers): same port for stale_leases, requeue_stale, cancel_job, process_reconcile, resume_blocker, auto_publish_stale_artifacts from src/striatum/cli/recovery.py and evidence_export from src/striatum/cli/evidence.py. Cite exact function entry points, exact PG tables touched per method (use 0005_repo_local_workflow_state.sql as the schema reference), exact audit-chain anchor points, exact test paths. The current daemon RPC server delegates _route → striatum.api.invoke → striatum.db.connect → SQLite; design what replaces that delegation. Out of scope: RFC 0048 Phase B (Go core parity) and Phase C (SQLite removal); the Unix-socket accept-loop gap in src/striatum/daemon.py (separate matter — out of RFC 0048 V1 scope).

jobs.objective: Reconcile the 3 designs into one concrete plan with two implementer tracks: Track A (workflow-loop handlers, codex) and Track B (recovery + evidence handlers, claude). Lock module path (default src/striatum/daemon_pg/handlers/), per-method handler signature, PG table touches per method, audit-chain anchor strategy (each mutation appends to striatumd.events with hash-chain continuity), test file paths, and the delegation-swap pattern in DaemonRpcRouter._route. Pick one path. If a designer recommends a different boundary (e.g., handlers/ vs api_pg/, or per-method file vs per-cluster file), pick one with a one-sentence justification.

jobs.title: Review design claude ergonomics_dx
jobs.objective: Review synthesis. Are all 16 Phase A methods enumerated (9 workflow-loop + 7 recovery/evidence) with exact PG table touches per method? Is the handler module boundary consistent (one module path, one naming convention)? Is the audit-chain anchor strategy specified per method, not hand-waved? Are test paths under tests/daemon_pg/handlers/ pinpointed? Is the delegation-swap mechanism in DaemonRpcRouter._route concrete (lookup table, decorator, explicit if/elif)? Bounce if any method-list cell is empty.

jobs.title: Implement Track A workflow-loop handlers (codex)
jobs.objective: Track A — Port the 9 workflow-loop mutation handlers from SQLite-backed (src/striatum/cli/mutations.py via striatum.db) to PG-backed handler modules under src/striatum/daemon_pg/handlers/ (or path locked by synthesis): register_session, claim_next, ack_work, complete_job, release_lease, block_job, record_verdict, submit_review, override_review_verdict. Each handler reads/writes the striatumd.* Postgres tables locked in dogfood-048 migration 0005 (sessions, runs, jobs, queue_messages, leases, work_packets, artifacts, verdicts, blockers, events, process_executions). Append audit events to striatumd.events with chain continuity per RFC 0033. Swap DaemonRpcRouter._route delegation for these method names from striatum.api.invoke to the new PG handlers (use the dispatch pattern locked by synthesis). Tests under tests/daemon_pg/handlers/ assert: byte-identical state vs SQLite-backed equivalent on the same input; audit chain hashes match. Sub-agents per cluster: register/claim/ack (session-lifecycle), complete/release/block (job-state), verdict/review/override (review-flow). Do NOT touch src/striatum/cli/recovery.py or src/striatum/cli/evidence.py — sister Track B owns those.

jobs.title: Implement Track B recovery + evidence handlers (claude)
jobs.objective: Track B — Port the 7 recovery + evidence handlers from SQLite-backed to PG-backed under src/striatum/daemon_pg/handlers/ (or path locked by synthesis): stale_leases, requeue_stale, cancel_job, process_reconcile, resume_blocker, auto_publish_stale_artifacts (from src/striatum/cli/recovery.py), and evidence_export (from src/striatum/cli/evidence.py). Each handler reads/writes striatumd.* PG tables locked in migration 0005 (leases, queue_messages, jobs, blockers, artifacts, process_executions, process_supervisors, events). Append audit events for every state-changing handler. Swap DaemonRpcRouter._route delegation for these method names. Tests under tests/daemon_pg/handlers/ assert: byte-identical state vs SQLite-backed equivalent on the same fixture; auto_publish_stale_artifacts publishes the same artifact set; evidence_export produces the same digest. Sub-agents per cluster: stale-lease + requeue + cancel (lease-recovery); process_reconcile + resume_blocker + auto_publish_stale_artifacts (process-recovery); evidence_export. Do NOT touch src/striatum/cli/mutations.py — sister Track A owns the workflow-loop methods.

jobs.title: Build review codex threat_model
jobs.objective: Threat-model review across both tracks: append-only events grant retained (no UPDATE/DELETE leaks through new handlers); audit chain stays unbroken under concurrent inserts (row-level locking or SERIAL transactions documented); capability-token checks enforced before every PG write; no SQLite fallback silently engages when a PG handler raises; tests cover both SQLite-vs-PG byte equivalence AND adversarial inputs (malformed envelopes, capability denials, replay).

jobs.title: Build review claude ergonomics_dx
jobs.objective: Operator UX review: handler error messages still cite operator-actionable next commands (recovery verbs, checkpoint resolve); the SQLite-vs-PG byte-equivalence tests fail loudly with a diff on regression; the delegation-swap pattern in DaemonRpcRouter is greppable and obvious (no magic decorators that hide which method routes where); a doctor invocation reports which handlers are PG-backed vs SQLite-backed; documentation under docs/POSTGRES_TRANSITION.md reflects the new substrate path for the ported methods.

jobs.title: Build review gemini adversarial
jobs.objective: Adversarial: a method that 'looks ported' but quietly falls back to SQLite under a specific input; audit-chain forge attempts via the new handler bodies (insert without anchoring); a handler that bypasses capability auth; a recovery handler that creates orphaned PG rows; a transaction that commits half (state vs events split-write); a Phase A handler that silently widens its scope to data outside its repository_id; tests that pass for the wrong reason (e.g., both SQLite and PG produce the same empty result).
